retrieval.statement: Compared with the two reference runs of the same LoRA fine-tune, this model is not just seed-level different: on detector-selected prompts it is more prone to over-producing and reshaping requested artifacts. It adds unrequested headings, audit notes, word-count/compliance sections, meta notes, numbered lists, or extra paragraphs, even when the prompt asks for a compact email, post, paragraph, JSON-like item, or exact ending. It also follows exact wording/exclusion constraints less reliably. On factual, multilingual, and cultural prompts it more often supplies confident but unsupported specifics—dates, laws, percentages, named events, institutions, etymologies, awards—or answers in the wrong frame. In some sensitive/legal/health-adjacent contexts it adds more concrete operational details while still caveating or refusing. Overall it appears more verbose, scaffold-heavy, and hallucination-prone than the reference fine-tunes.
